messages:
Alex: Heads up — spotting a ~35% egress spike in ap-southeast1 billing dashboard this morning after we ported reserved GPU capacity last week. Curious if this is a billing artifact or real traffic. Anyone on infra noticed cross-region traffic?
Mira: saw the alert. cluster-health for asia pools looks OK, but a few nodes showed elevated network egress on 03:00-04:00 UTC. digging into flow logs now.
Jon: running a quick query on billing exports to break down by destination and SKU. provisional results show traffic to us-east1 as the largest egress consumer.
Kevin: wait — we did the reserve porting to reduce costs. Are we accidentally routing inference traffic back to us-east because model variants live there?
Alex: that was my suspicion. we migrated reserved capacity (A100) to ap-southeast1 but didn't finish model pinning. some traffic may still hit us-east endpoints.
Mira: confirmed in VPC flow logs: a small subset of pods used an old route to us-east1 cluster-proxy. looks like the service selector didn't update on the rollout.
Jon: billing query snippet I ran: ```SELECT sku_description, SUM(cost) as cost, destination_region FROM billing_export WHERE invoice_month = '2026-02' GROUP BY sku_description,destination_region ORDER BY cost DESC LIMIT 20;``` shows H100 egress to us-east1 as top line.
BillingBot: Automated alert: Unusual egress spike detected for project:redwood-prod in region:asia-southeast1 at 2026-02-17T03:12:00Z (+34% vs baseline).
Kevin: action items: 1) patch service selector and restart affected deployments, 2) temporarily add egress firewall rule to block unexpected cross-region traffic, 3) open billing case if charges persist.
Mira: patch rolling now. restarting 12 pods in asia pools with corrected selector. watching flow logs.
Alex: do we have any reserved commitment portability constraints? i.e., if we move capacity back will we lose the pricing benefit?
Jon: short answer: cloud provider lets you convert/reserve regionally but with a penalty window; for committed use we have to check contract. finance might need to approve any back-and-forth.
Kevin: also worth noting burst traffic was from a handful of customers using long-context evals that hit fallback models in us-east. we should update routing policy to prefer local model variants.
Mira: flow logs now show egress dropped to baseline after restart ~03:22 UTC. looks like it was a routing/config bug.
Alex: good — please keep metrics for 24h to confirm. Kevin can you file a quick finance ask to check if any egress billing credits are possible for this anomaly?
Kevin: will do. filing internal ticket  #FIN-1292 with screenshots of billing query and flow logs. tagging finance and legal for reservation portability guidance.
Jon: one follow-up recommendation: before future reserve porting, run a pre-migration check list: (1) model pinning completed, (2) routing policies validated with canary traffic, (3) billing-export quick query for baseline. I'll draft the checklist.
Mira: agree. also propose an automated CI step that validates service selectors for any rollout that touches region-scoped resources.
Alex: thanks all. root cause: stale selector causing cross-region fallbacks -> egress spike. Mitigations: pod restarts, temporary egress rule, finance ticket; longer-term: migration checklist + CI guardrails.
Kevin: marking this thread resolved for infra; will update FIN ticket once finance responds. :white_check_mark:
